purpose: Phase-8A deterministic population-enrichment model. Given selection pressure + differential subpopulation response, it produces conserved fraction changes that redistribute the normalized population toward less-sensitive subpopulations. CRITICAL distinctions: (1) enrichment CONSERVES the normalized composition (sum stays 1.0); (2) relative resistant enrichment is NOT the same as absolute tumour growth - a resistant fraction may RISE while total tumour burden FALLS. Schematic only.

coefficient_policy.valid_range: enrichment_strength in [0,1]; fraction changes are conserved (sum of changes = 0)
coefficient_policy.1_interpretation: 1 = maximal schematic enrichment step the model represents
coefficient_policy.sensitivity_note: enrichment_step scales the per-frame redistribution; larger values enrich faster but never break conservation.
coefficient_policy.limitations: No absolute count change; relative composition only (NOT_REPORTED quantitatively).

rules.conservation: Sum of all fraction changes each frame is 0 (within tolerance); no fraction leaves [0,1].
rules.selection_vs_growth: Enrichment describes relative composition, decoupled from absolute tumour burden; documentation and runtime preserve that a resistant fraction can increase while burden decreases.
rules.de_enrichment_allowed: Where biologically supported (e.g. re-sensitization / tolerance resolution), fractions may shift BACK toward sensitive; this is de-enrichment, still conserved.
